summary: Build practical cyber governance skills for public institutions with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, COBIT 2019, and board-ready reporting.
lede: Cybersecurity governance for public institutions provides a structured way to direct, oversee, assess, and report on cyber risk. This course shows you how to connect policies, decision rights, assurance activities, escalation routes, and performance measures under ISO/IEC 27001:2022, COBIT 2019, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0. You will practise creating a governance scorecard, assigning control responsibilities, developing a cyber risk register, preparing board briefings, and identifying governance gaps. You will also explore AI-assisted analytics dashboards and automated control-monitoring workflows at an operational level, helping you coordinate oversight across ICT, audit, legal, and procurement functions despite limited capacity, legacy systems, fragmented inventories, and uneven data quality.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work inside public-sector governance, ICT, risk, audit, or service-management functions and need a practical way to govern cyber risk.
prerequisites: Intermediate experience in public administration, ICT governance, risk management, internal audit, information security, or compliance is recommended. You should be comfortable reading governance policies, incident reports, and control summaries, but no programming is required. Familiarity with basic cybersecurity concepts, asset management, and public-sector reporting structures will help you get more from the exercises. Bring a laptop for workshop templates, and be prepared to work with sample registers, dashboards, and governance matrices.
